items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: he came and sat in with Jack Sheldon and myself at the Money Tree last Sunday

ctx.x: It was the first time in 30 years. He got his trumpet, he went to Uan Rasey for a week, and he came and sat in with Jack Sheldon and myself at the Money Tree last Sunday
night. He said, “This is the first time I’ve played in 30 years.” He got himself a brand new beautiful trumpet.

items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: And I work at Chadney’s every Sunday night with Ross Tompkins, we do a duet.

ctx.x: Is the live jazz scene healthy around here or not?

Yeah it always has been for me. I always work good and there’s a place called Steamers, a great club in Fullerton wherever that is, somewhere way out somewhere. I worked there. We’re going to record there in April. And I work at Chadney’s every Sunday night with Ross Tompkins, we do a duet. And then I work with the big band and work different

places with the quartet: Spagitinni’s and different clubs, the Catalinas in Hollywood, and I work sometimes with Jeff Goldblum, with a movie star band, with Peter Weller plays trumpet and Jeff Goldblum plays piano.
